effect: The oxygen-bearing cells and plasma mixture formed blood, completing the chapter goal.
reaction: The final picture brings the distinct blood components together clearly.

mostWorthwhile.text: Binding oxygen to red cells was most worthwhile: the planned inset and explanation show that haemoglobin can both bind and release oxygen, especially where dissolved oxygen is lower.

leastWorthwhile.text: Trying to add red cells to the plasma mixture was confusing: the mixture had no available combination, although red cells normally circulate in plasma.

surprise.text: The first attempt to combine plasma with red cells instead automatically added white cells and platelets.

arbitrary.text: Requiring oxygen to be added to red cells before assembling the blood sample felt arbitrary; the supplied explanation did not establish why that order was necessary.

continue.text: I would continue: the oxygen-binding explanation was useful, and I would be interested to see how circulation brings oxygen carriers close to tissues, though the restrictive combination order was frustrating.
